title: Remarks at Edgeley, N.D
paragraphs: I am very glad to see you and I am glad to be back [?] again in North Dakota, and to be greeted as you are greeting me to-night. It was [?] twenty three years ago that I first set foot in North Dakota, and for a number of years I lived my life out in the western part of the state; and I have most naturally a peculiar feeling for its people. It does me good to see you. You are a great state, a stock-growing state in the west and a great wheat raising state here; but the reasons I like you most are the men and women, and in addition to the men and women I am glad to see there are a few children down here too. You seem to be all right in quantity of children and all right in quality, and I am glad of that, because I think it is a good stock and I do not want to see it die out.. (Cheers and applause)

diplomatic: My Friends and Fellow Citizens:

I am very glad to see you and I am glad to be here back again in North Dakota, and to be greeted as you are greeting me to-night. It is was twenty three years ago that I first set foot in North Dakota, and for a number of years I lived my life out in the western part of the state; and I have most naturally a peculiar feeling for xxx its people. It does me good to see you. You are a great state, a stock-growing state in the west and still a great wheat raising state here; but the reasons I like you most are the men and women, and in addition to the men and women I am glad to see there are a few children down here too .
